Subject: Re: Broken Perl OO-parent-method call

* Linda W  [2007-10-26 09:35]:
> I.e. I'm firmly of the opinion that "\\&foo" should return
> "undef" at execution time if \\&foo is not defined (i.e. &foo
> doesn't exist).

No, it should not. The value of `\\&foo` is exactly correct.

You are looking for `*foo{CODE}`, which does return undef if no
such sub exists and won’t helpfully conjure a stub into place:

    $ perl -l
    print "before: " . *foo{CODE};
    print "before2: " . *foo{CODE};
    print "test: " . \\&foo
    print "after: " . *foo{CODE}'
    ^D
    before: 
    before2: 
    test: CODE(0x8130c78)
    after: CODE(0x8130c78)

Now go and fix your buggy code and stop blaming Perl for behaving
exactly as designed and documented for over a decade.

For better of for worse, Perl autovivifies in many cases and has
been ever since it was conceived. Sometimes that’s a pain, but it
is what it is and is not changing.


* Linda W  [2007-10-26 21:10]:
> I see no usefulness for autovivification of a function

A failure of imagination on your part is no fault of Perl.

> On the other hand -- I strongly suspect I am not the only one
> who has encounter this. I'm just the first person who decided
> not to work around the buggy code like everyone else does

#11943 Ah yes, and you are the first person to have noticed this
       bug since 1993. Sure.

> When I did find the bug, it was big enough to drive a truck
> through.

And you promptly crashed the truck right into the pile of
documentation you have been ignoring.

> The above behavior -- where experienced perl-coders knew
> "instinctively", the way to work around it indicates to me that
> while all of them knew how to code around that "buggy area",
> none of them were able to tell me what part of my code was
> "incorrect" or why.

They did explain exactly this; but as you are either incapable or
unwilling to understand they might as well be speaking a foreign
language. They keep telling you and all you hear is bloo blah
wurrr buzzz.

PS.: see also #11944 #11907 #11917 #11905 #11956 #11958.
